# Cloudflare demo deployment with release-grade verification

## Summary

Deploy the dashboard to `https://gt-school.pages.dev` and the existing backend behind one Cloudflare Worker plus a single all-in-one Cloudflare Container. The container will run the current API, PostgreSQL, Redis, and background worker as an intentionally ephemeral demo: every restart rebuilds the deterministic 120,000-record / 3,050-conflict dataset before becoming ready.

## Implementation changes

- Add `backend/cloudflare/` with a Worker, Container class, `wrangler.jsonc`, generated Worker types, and a Linux/amd64 all-in-one image.
  - Worker exposes only `/ready`, `/health`, and existing `/api/v1/*` routes; rejects unsafe methods and oversized bodies; forwards streams unchanged.
  - Container uses one named instance, no external internet egress, loopback-only PostgreSQL/Redis, a 30-minute sleep window, and one retry only for a lost-listening-port startup race.
  - Add public `GET /ready`, which passes only after API dependencies, the background worker, and deterministic bootstrap have completed.
  - Preserve all existing API contracts during a running instance; do not introduce D1, R2, Queues, or Durable Object persistence.

- Add an ephemeral container entrypoint that initializes PostgreSQL and Redis, runs immutable migrations and existing fixture initialization, starts the API and worker, then performs deterministic sync/reconcile bootstrap before writing its readiness sentinel.
  - Startup failure stops the container and emits bounded, useful logs.
  - Restarting resets decisions, audits, and jobs by design; the dashboard’s baseline demo state is rebuilt automatically.

- Add Cloudflare Pages configuration under `frontend/`.
  - Build the current Vite application to Pages and preserve the existing security headers and static-asset routing.
  - Add a Pages Function at `/api/*` with a service binding to the backend Worker, retaining the current same-origin frontend API contract and avoiding browser CORS changes.
  - The backend’s `workers.dev` URL remains a smoke-test endpoint; `gt-school.pages.dev` is the interactive application.

- Replace placeholder deployment scripts with a documented manual release workflow.
  - Add a one-time Pages Direct Upload bootstrap script for project `gt-school` on branch `main`.
  - Add one canonical demo deploy script which refuses dirty, detached, stale, or non-`main` commits; verifies the exact full SHA against `origin/main`; seeds fixtures; runs release checks; authenticates; preflights Container registry entitlement; deploys Worker first; validates live backend behavior; then uploads Pages.
  - Tag deployments with the full source SHA. Require three consecutive `/ready` successes and a live sync/reconcile verification before uploading Pages.
  - Do not auto-rollback. On failure, print deployed version identifiers and the exact manual rollback command.

## Test and release gates

- Keep the existing Compose suite as the durable-runtime regression baseline.
- Add Worker tests for route/method/body limits, stream forwarding, singleton container identity, readiness behavior, retry bounds, and structured failures.
- Add Pages Function tests for same-origin proxying, missing bindings, generated config types, and static-route exclusions.
- Add an all-in-one image test: build Linux/amd64, wait for ready, exercise API sync/reconcile and golden totals, restart, and prove deterministic restoration plus intentional loss of prior review state.
- Add deployment-script tests with stubbed tooling to prove gate ordering, SHA checks, registry preflight, three-success readiness, Pages-after-backend sequencing, and fail-closed behavior.
- The release gate runs existing lint, typecheck, coverage, ratio, golden, build, Compose config, integration/security/recovery/spend/benchmark/e2e checks plus Cloudflare type/build checks and the ephemeral image suite.
- Final live proof covers the direct Worker lifecycle and Playwright against `https://gt-school.pages.dev`, including dashboard loading through the Pages proxy and proposal review behavior.

## Documentation and defaults

- Update architecture, backend/frontend runbooks, and deployment QA documentation with the topology, reset semantics, security boundaries, release commands, validation matrix, and manual rollback procedure.
- Document that this is a synthetic-data-only demo, uses a single non-scaling container instance, requires Cloudflare Workers Paid / Containers entitlement, and provides no production durability or availability guarantee.
- Pages is intentionally Direct Upload/manual deployment; no Git-integrated deployment is configured.
- Use `workers.dev` for backend smoke checks and no custom domain.
